entries.author: kgraves
entries.cardQuote: This is how the scam begins, the downfall of Solana. It is yet another pump and dump just like all of these coins.
entries.quote: This is how the scam begins, the downfall of Solana. It is yet another pump and dump just like all of these coins. Cryptocurrencies must be stopped, there is absolutely NO benefit to having them. We seen them all before, ransomware becoming rampant, massive waste of electricity and resources and now the pandora's box can't be closed quicker enough.
entries.storyTitle: Solana Labs completes a $314M private token sale led by Andreessen Horowitz
entries.outcome: Solana became a top-10 blockchain with a spot ETF and a large DeFi and NFT economy.
entries.outcomeDetail: Solana's mainnet launched in 2020 and survived repeated outages to become one of the most-used smart-contract networks. SOL is a top-10 asset, spot SOL ETFs began trading in 2025, and Solana hosts billions of dollars in DeFi activity.
entries.note: kgraves saw a generic altcoin pump-and-dump. Solana instead became one of the few chains with real retail, developer and ETF demand.

entries.author: nootropicat
entries.cardQuote: Solana fails on both, most egregiously on the latter. Only 4.3% of coins were even offered in a public sale. The idea that defi can run on a chain controlled entirely by few VCs is ridiculous.
entries.quote: Decentralization needs two properties at once: - ability for the system to run entirely in people's home. Anything that requires datacenters can be easily regulated. - distributed holdings with no entity holding more than few percent at most. Solana fails on both, most egregiously on the latter. Only 4.3% of coins were even offered in a public sale. The idea that defi can run on a chain controlled entirely by few VCs is ridiculous. Even Libra would be preferable with their Swiss based Libra Association. https://icodrops.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Solano-token...
entries.storyTitle: Solana Labs completes a $314M private token sale led by Andreessen Horowitz
entries.outcome: Solana became a top-10 chain and a major DeFi hub despite its concentrated token distribution.
entries.outcomeDetail: Solana's early token sale was indeed concentrated, and the network drew persistent criticism over validator costs and outages. It nonetheless grew into one of the largest smart-contract platforms, with a top-10 native asset and billions in DeFi value.
entries.note: nootropicat was right that the supply was concentrated and the hardware demands were high. He was wrong that DeFi could not run on the chain; Solana's DeFi and NFT activity became substantial.

entries.quote: Agree completely. Nice paper, utterly useless in practice due to sybil attack. edit: not only that, but it will be vulnerable to all kinds of history attacks for bootstrapping nodes
entries.storyTitle: Snowflake to Avalanche: A Novel Metastable Consensus Protocol Family for Crypto
entries.outcome: Avalanche launched in 2020 and became a top-25 blockchain with subnets and institutional pilots.
entries.outcomeDetail: The Snowflake-to-Avalanche consensus paper became the basis for Ava Labs' Avalanche network, launched in September 2020. AVAX remains a top-25 asset, and Avalanche has been used for subnets, tokenized assets and enterprise experiments.
entries.note: wildbunny dismissed the consensus paper as unusable because of Sybil attacks. Ava Labs built a staked validator set around the protocol and shipped a live, valuable network.

entries.author: Jasper_
entries.cardQuote: My guess is that Bitfinex, through a combination of wash trading and Tethers, have been pushing up the price of Bitcoin and they've basically been running a Ponzi scheme.
entries.quote: Who gave them all that USD? Where are they keeping it? They've been shunned by their US banking partners. They've basically been printing Tethers 50m at a time. The only thing they've released which attempted to show that they actually had the USD was something they called an "audit" which explicitly said "this is not an audit" ... on the second page. When you go to withdraw from Tethers it basically says "if you don't have more than $50k in claims, go away" ... Suffice it to say that most of their customers don't have that. My guess is that Bitfinex, through a combination of wash trading and Tethers, have been pushing up the price of Bitcoin and they've basically been running a Ponzi scheme.
entries.outcome: Tether survived, became the largest stablecoin, and settled reserve-related cases with regulators.
entries.outcomeDetail: Tether did not collapse. USDT grew into the largest stablecoin by market cap and trading volume, while Tether paid $41 million to the CFTC in 2021 and $18.5 million to the New York attorney general over its reserve disclosures.
entries.note: Jasper_ was right that Tether's reserves were opaque and its attestations were weak. The predicted Ponzi collapse never came; USDT became the plumbing of offshore crypto trading.

entries.author: patio11
entries.cardQuote: Hilarity then ensues, for values of hilarity which probably mean "bank run" on a bank which is structurally incapable of paying out most holders of money.
entries.quote: If you haven't been following along, here's why this matters: Tethers is a sole-source cryptocurrency, pegged to the US dollar. Bitfinex produces it, though they're cagey (some would say outright lying at times) about the level of involvement. The primary purpose of tethers is money laundering, even more so than cryptocurrency generally. Bitfinex was cut off from the US financial system, which makes it impossible for them to clear USD-denominated wires. Their clients have ~$400M of USD on deposit with Bitfinex. Their solution: issue a cryptocurrency which is claimed to be 100% backed by USD and say that it is redeemable 1-to-1 for dollars... we just can't actually physically give you the dollars. Incredibly, this has worked so far. Bitfinex has issued approximately $600 million in tethers, all but $10 million or so in the last 6 months. They're usable on a handful of exchanges, for the purpose of buying BTC and other cryptocurrencies. Tether claims that someone has stolen 5% or so of their $600 million tethers -- the digital claims, not the underlying dollars sitting at their totally-exists-we-promise bank account. They've made a technological change to the Omni client to disallow transactions on the stolen tokens, but there is no guarantee that they succeed in convincing all parties to use this. The nightmare scenario for them is 1+ exchanges say "Well, actually, we rely on your money actually being money to list it here, so pick: we delist you or we don't, but we don't have any incentive to apply that patch." ... The thief immediately exfiltrates to Bitcoin, and suddenly 30 million hot tethers are contaminating the money stream at the exchange, and they cannot be conveniently disambiguated from clean tethers, because money is fungible. Hilarity then ensues, for values of hilarity which probably mean "bank run" on a bank which is structurally incapable of paying out most holders of money. ... Why does Bitfinex care whether their cryptocurrency is listed at other exchanges? Because they need to launder money to support their exchange business. Tethers are institutionalizing a sort of crypto-hawala (or crypto-Liberty Reserve), allowing the physical transfer of real money to happen at legal remoteness to the cryptocurrency exchange. Bitfinex has an order book filled with something people want. A way to get access to that orderbook is to say "Bitfinex, I want some tether, how do you sell them to me if you can't accept a wire?" Bitfinex might say "Are you a trustworthy US VC? Spiffy. Move $20 million from your left hand pocket to your right hand pocket. The right hand pocket is now ours; here's $20 to $21 million in Tether, which are good for BTC at your favorite exchanges. At some time in the future, a trustworthy US VC other than yourself is going to ask you to buy some tether from them at par value. You will do that, and pay them from your right pocket. If a regulator asks you about this transaction, you bat your eyes and say 'Oh, sophisticated investors doing a cryptocurrency transaction, nothing to see here.'" Post-script: Is this good news for Bitcoin? Oh this is great news for Bitcoin. If you don't believe Bitfinex's $600 million in liabilities are worth a copper shilling, the only option for getting your value out of Bitfinex is to swap your liability for Bitcoin, which drives up the price of Bitcoin at the margin. This is exactly what happened in the final months of Mt. Gox.
entries.outcome: USDT became the largest stablecoin and survived the 2022 stablecoin run.
entries.outcomeDetail: Tether's opacity was real, and regulators fined it over its reserve claims. But USDT kept its dollar peg through the 2022 Terra and FTX stress and grew to roughly $175 billion in circulation by 2026.
entries.note: patio11's bank-run framework was the right way to think about Tether. The run never became fatal because USDT was too deeply embedded in crypto trading to fail without taking the market with it.

entries.author: rebuilder
entries.cardQuote: You can try to build a complicated system to hide all that, but it seems the goal of a stable peg is simply impossible.
entries.quote: It seems to me that any decentralized stablecoin would break the impossible trinity. [0] Basically, since the interest rate is fixed (at 0 in this case, I believe), there's an incentive to sell DAI in favour of some higher-yielding currency, which creates a downward pressure on the price. So short of preventing DAI from being sold somehow, in order to maintain a peg, someone needs to pump money into DAI at a loss. You can try to build a complicated system to hide all that, but it seems the goal of a stable peg is simply impossible. Even for nation states it is only possible in the case they have sufficient resources and the will to maintain a peg. [0]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impossible_trinity
entries.storyTitle: MakerDAO’s “DAI” stablecoin is breaking, as predicted
entries.outcome: DAI became the largest decentralized stablecoin and held its peg through multiple crypto crashes.
entries.outcomeDetail: MakerDAO's DAI grew into the largest decentralized stablecoin, surviving the March 2020 crash and the 2022 bear market. Maker rebranded as Sky in 2024; DAI and its USDS successor together held billions in supply.
entries.note: rebuilder applied the impossible trinity to DAI and concluded a peg could not hold. DAI's overcollateralization and liquidation mechanics kept it near $1 for years.

entries.author: pjbyrne
entries.cardQuote: They are claiming the system "ensures" that the stablecoin is "a money that will always maintain its purchasing power." "Ensure" and 'always' don't mean "trend towards over time." They mean always, as in all the time.
entries.quote: > They are claiming that over a sufficient period of time the coin will trend towards its target This is not what the MakerDAO team, nor any other stablecoin shill, is claiming. They are claiming the system "ensures" that the stablecoin is "a money that will always maintain its purchasing power." "Ensure" and 'always' don't mean "trend towards over time." They mean always, as in all the time. If their intention is to sell a different product, I can only suggest they make more representations which are a little harder to falsify.
entries.storyTitle: MakerDAO’s “DAI” stablecoin is breaking, as predicted
entries.outcome: DAI survived but did briefly trade off peg during market stress.
entries.outcomeDetail: DAI became the leading decentralized stablecoin and usually traded within a cent of $1. It still slipped during the March 2020 crash and the 2023 USDC depeg, so the absolutist marketing claim was falsified even though the system held.
entries.note: pjbyrne attacked the marketing absolutism rather than the mechanism. DAI did drift off peg under stress, but it did not break, which is why the project outlived the critique.

entries.author: qeternity
entries.cardQuote: Every other exchange which already has dumb retail money and fiat on ramps will eat their lunch. FTX, Coinbase, etc
entries.quote: Every other exchange which already has dumb retail money and fiat on ramps will eat their lunch. FTX, Coinbase, etc
entries.outcome: OpenSea remained the largest NFT marketplace by users; Coinbase shut its NFT marketplace and FTX collapsed.
entries.outcomeDetail: OpenSea stayed the default NFT marketplace through the 2022 downturn. Coinbase launched its NFT marketplace in 2022 and sunset it in 2024; FTX collapsed in November 2022. OpenSea later relaunched as OS2 and regained NFT market share, though Blur led trading volume for a stretch.
entries.note: qeternity expected centralized exchanges to crush OpenSea. The exchanges had distribution but not the NFT supply or culture, and their marketplaces flopped.

entries.author: Maarten88
entries.cardQuote: I can understand that Bitcoin and Ethereum have value, but I have a hard time understanding why Ripple (XRP) has the value it has.
entries.quote: He does have a point. I can understand that Bitcoin and Ethereum have value, but I have a hard time understanding why Ripple (XRP) has the value it has. The way I understand it: - Ripple offers blockchain software aimed at banks, who use it for transaction settlement. These banks will use a private blockchain, obviously, that is separate from XRP. - XRP are pre-mined. Ripple investors and team owned all 100B of them at the start. They can sell them off slowly, as long as there is enough demand at the current price they'll all be billionaires. I think Ripple have two good things going, but buying XRP seems like too good a deal for them, not so much for the buyer.
entries.storyTitle: Ripple co-founder fifth richest person in US, rivaling Zuckerberg
entries.outcome: XRP remained a top-10 asset, won its SEC case, and returned above $3 in 2025.
entries.outcomeDetail: The SEC sued Ripple in December 2020; a judge ruled in 2023 that XRP sold on public exchanges was not a security, and the SEC ended the case in 2025. XRP stayed in the top 10 by market cap and traded above $3 in 2025, near its 2018 peak.
entries.note: Maarten88 could not see where XRP's value came from beyond Ripple's bank software. The market kept valuing the token, and the legal cloud lifted without killing it.

entries.author: EduardoBautista
entries.cardQuote: As long as people have the need to pay in regular currencies, decentralized exchanges aren't an alternative to Coinbase, Kraken, etc.
entries.quote: Exactly. As long as people have the need to pay in regular currencies, decentralized exchanges aren't an alternative to Coinbase, Kraken, etc.
entries.outcome: Uniswap became the first DEX to top $3 trillion in cumulative volume and remains a leading on-chain exchange.
entries.outcomeDetail: Uniswap v3 launched in May 2021 and became the dominant automated market maker. By 2025 Uniswap had processed more than $3 trillion in cumulative trading volume, and UNI remained one of the largest DeFi tokens.
entries.note: EduardoBautista was right that fiat on-ramps remain a centralized chokepoint. But DEXs became a real alternative for on-chain trading, and Uniswap captured trillions in volume.

entries.author: jki275
entries.cardQuote: Chainlink is a scam. Other than that, there's a ton of hype and BS in the cryptocurrency world, lots of Ponzi schemes and fraud.
entries.quote: Chainlink is a scam. Other than that, there's a ton of hype and BS in the cryptocurrency world, lots of Ponzi schemes and fraud. That's where a lot of negative opinion comes from.
entries.storyTitle: Ask HN: Why is HN so aggressively anti-Bitcoin?
entries.outcome: Chainlink became the dominant oracle network, securing DeFi and partnering with major financial infrastructure.
entries.outcomeDetail: Chainlink's price feeds became the standard oracle layer for DeFi, and its CCIP cross-chain protocol was used in pilots with banks and market infrastructure. LINK remained one of the largest crypto assets.
entries.note: jki275 filed Chainlink under the same category as the era's scams. It became the infrastructure that much of DeFi, and later tokenized finance, relied on.

entries.author: davidgerard
entries.cardQuote: The software is just another DPOS blockchain with smart contracts - it doesn't do anything much better than the multiple other such pseudo-decentralised blockchains. The only point was to support a token offering.
entries.quote: You think it's bad, I've still got "Telephone" stuck in my head every time I hear about the Telegram blockchain. But you know what they say: a pain shared is a pain doubled! The software is just another DPOS blockchain with smart contracts - it doesn't do anything much better than the multiple other such pseudo-decentralised blockchains. The only point was to support a token offering.
entries.storyTitle: Telegram gives up on the Telegram Open Network
entries.outcome: Telegram abandoned TON, but the community revived it; Toncoin became a top-30 asset integrated into Telegram wallets.
entries.outcomeDetail: Telegram gave up on TON in 2020 after the SEC blocked Gram. The open-source network was revived as The Open Network, and Toncoin grew into a top-30 cryptocurrency; Telegram later integrated TON-based wallets and mini-apps.
entries.note: davidgerard was right that Telegram's original TON was a token vehicle with little differentiation. He was wrong that the software had no life after Telegram; the community fork found a real distribution channel in Telegram's user base.

entries.author: rushsteve1
entries.cardQuote: I can't seem to figure out what Cardano offers that existing, and well established, cryptocurrencies like Ethereum don't.
entries.quote: While the concept of a peer-reviewed cryptocurrency is an interesting one, and certainly has merit, I can't seem to figure out what Cardano offers that existing, and well established, cryptocurrencies like Ethereum don't.
entries.storyTitle: What is Cardano? An introduction to the cryptocurrency being built by scientists
entries.outcome: Cardano shipped smart contracts and briefly became a top-3 asset, but by 2026 it had fallen to #18.
entries.outcomeDetail: Cardano launched smart contracts via the Alonzo upgrade in 2021, and ADA peaked above $3, briefly making it a top-3 cryptocurrency. By late 2026 ADA had fallen to roughly #18 with a market cap around $6 billion, and its DeFi ecosystem remained much smaller than Ethereum's.
entries.note: rushsteve1 could not see the differentiation, and the market eventually agreed on usage even after a huge speculative run. The 2017 dismissal still missed how far the token would climb first.

entries.author: _9omd
entries.cardQuote: the writing is on the wall for this project long term. It's going to get absolutely crushed when real L2s like optimism... get significant adoption
entries.quote: I made a nice 4x return riding the Polygon hype, but the writing is on the wall for this project long term. It's going to get absolutely crushed when real L2s like optimism, atribturm, zksync, starkware, etc. get significant adoption (likely by this summer). The meme of it being a better BSC allowed easy dapp porting and a quick surge of liquidity, but just being a better BSC is not nearly good enough long term. Liquidity can flow out of Polygon just as quickly as it flowed in when better solutions are available. I think their somewhat recent branding from Matic to Polygon was a distraction ploy to get users to think they'll be competitive in the true L2 space and grow beyond just having a seperate POS chain. They keep saying how they're not just one scaling solution, but a suite of scaling solutions, yet have released no evidence of any progress on implementing rollups. From what I can see right now, it seems highly unlikely the team will have any kind of working rollup in the near future. Rollups are still bleeding edge tech, and most of the code from the teams battling in the space is closed source. As far as I'm aware Polygon outsources most of its dev work, while other L2 teams are stacked with industry veterans with deep knowledge in applied cryptography. Once enough of the rollup tech becomes open source, Polygon can copy it, but by that time it'll likely be far too late.
entries.outcome: Polygon raised $450M from Sequoia, Tiger and SoftBank and remained a major scaling ecosystem, but POL fell to about #62 by 2026.
entries.outcomeDetail: Polygon kept building: it launched zkEVM, acquired several zero-knowledge teams, and replaced MATIC with POL in 2024. Sequoia, Tiger Global and SoftBank had invested $450 million in 2022. But by November 2026 POL traded near $0.08 with a market cap under $1 billion, while Arbitrum, Base and Optimism dominated L2 activity.
entries.note: _9omd was early and right about the risk: Polygon's sidechain model and outsourced rollup work left it exposed once real L2s scaled. The network survived, but the token did not escape the crush he predicted.

entries.author: prepend
entries.cardQuote: they are all unregulated, not fdic insured, and seem to survive on bitcoin's ever increasing rise... not being audited is such a terrible signal.
entries.quote: This seems so common to me and it’s surprising how many of these ventures are around. And that they haven’t busted yet. I looked at these a few years ago when the 5%+ returns started popping up and they are all unregulated, not fdic insured, and seem to survive on bitcoin’s ever increasing rise. If these returns were true then institutional investors would use them. But they do seem like they should have collapsed years ago. Maybe they aren’t run by scam artists but by people who earnestly believe that they can make money by mining and pawn it off as returns. But not being audited is such a terrible signal. It’s weird that anyone would genuinely buy into these.
entries.storyTitle: The biggest crypto lending company is a ponzi scheme
entries.outcome: Celsius froze withdrawals in June 2022, filed for bankruptcy, and its founder was sentenced to 12 years.
entries.outcomeDetail: Celsius paused all withdrawals in June 2022 and filed for Chapter 11 the next month. Founder Alex Mashinsky pleaded guilty to fraud and was sentenced to 12 years in prison in May 2025.
entries.note: prepend went beyond the Ponzi label: he described the entire unaudited yield model as structurally doomed, with no deposit insurance and no way to survive a crypto drawdown. Celsius froze customer funds within seven months.

entries.author: Uptrenda
entries.cardQuote: It's only real claim to fame is that it copy-pasted the code earlier than most other cryptocurrencies and hence now survives as a zombie currency backed by the souls of all the bag-holders foolish enough to invest in it
entries.quote: I never really got the appeal of Litecoin. It was basically just a copy and paste of Bitcoin with only minor alterations made to the source code (like changing the PoW for Script which never really defeated ASICs and a few other small changes.) It made no major innovations that can be named and even to this day it still lacks several of the major bug fixes that made it into Bitcoin (there are still patches missing from like ~2014 that result in the software being even harder to use for devs than Bitcoin.) This is not coming from a Bitcoin Maximalist, by the way (not presently a fan of Bitcoin either.) Just thought I'd point out how bizarre it is that Litecoin even has a price at all when the software is functionally similar to Dogecoin. It's only real claim to fame is that it copy-pasted the code earlier than most other cryptocurrencies and hence now survives as a zombie currency backed by the souls of all the bag-holders foolish enough to invest in it (much like how Yahoo continues to survive to this day.) Can we all just agree that Litecoin is a way over-hyped and silly excuse for a cryptocurrency? Silver to Bitcoin's gold? I can't think of a single problem that Litecoin actually solves compared to ... well, anything. At best: you could say its a speculative instrument tied to the cancerous block size debate. But other than that - is good marketing really worth the price of $21 USD a coin? I can see a lot of people getting screwed by this when the currency inevitably crashes again ...
entries.outcome: Litecoin survived and got a U.S. spot ETF in 2025, but never regained its 2017 peak.
entries.outcomeDetail: Litecoin kept running as one of the oldest Bitcoin forks and won a U.S. spot ETF listing in October 2025. LTC traded around $60 in 2026, far below its 2017 high near $400, and remained a small payments and speculation asset.
entries.note: Uptrenda was harsh but largely right about the technology: Litecoin added little that Bitcoin did not have. The 'zombie currency' survived, which is exactly the outcome he described.
